comparisons.peer_topic: Net interest income and yield performance in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income decreased by $871 million to $56.1 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, with net interest yield on a fully taxable-equivalent basis dropping 13 basis points to 1.95 percent. These declines were primarily driven by higher deposit costs, which were partially offset by higher asset yields and increased net interest income from Global Markets activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Bank of America disclosed changes in net interest income driven by a combination of volume shifts and rate/cost pressures, though the net outcomes differed. Citigroup reported a 1% increase in net interest income, boosted by higher deposit and loan volumes but offset by declining rates in Argentina. In contrast, Bank of America reported a decrease of $871 million in net interest income, primarily driven by higher deposit costs and lower average loan balances, which were only partially offset by higher net interest income from Global Markets activity. Both firms cited offsetting dynamics involving rates/costs versus volume/market activities, but C benefited from volume growth while BAC suffered from margin compression and loan balance declines.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net Interest Income Growth and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income for 2024 was $8.06 billion, representing a 27% increase from 2023, driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates, partially offset by a decrease in deposits with banks.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs analyzed net interest income dynamics as a result of offsetting factors between income drivers and expense/rate environments. Goldman Sachs reported a 27% increase in net interest income to $8.06 billion, driven by higher interest income from trading assets and investments (benefiting from higher balances and rates), partially offset by a decrease in interest income from deposits with banks. Similarly, Citigroup reported a 1% increase in net interest income, driven by higher deposit and loan volumes but offset by declining interest rates in Argentina. Both firms saw their primary income drivers (trading assets/investments for GS; loans/deposits for C) supported by volume or favorable rate movements, but faced headwinds from other segments or regions (deposits with banks for GS; Argentina for C).
